target_customer: Event organizers and sponsors who want more engaged rooms, plus attendees who want to meet people at events they already attend
problem: Attendees at events rarely know who else is in the room or how to follow up with the people they want to meet. Organizers want engagement and sponsors want an audience that showed up on purpose.
business_model: Freemium consumer networking with premium app features, plus organizer and sponsor offerings tied to events (Eventbrite integration)

founders.name: André Woodley Jr.
previous_startups: Mobile on-demand music platform he says reached 500,000 users (self-reported, outcome not stated)
Two-person AI startup he says he exited (self-reported)
founders.background_notes: The YC page describes him as a sole founder with a software engineering, growth and design background. No employers or schools are listed, so those are null. A Crunchbase snippet lists him as co-founder of Qwest (YC W19), which this research did not open or verify.

competitors.name: Brella
competitors.what: Mobile and web app that matches business event attendees with relevant contacts using an algorithm
competitors.funding_then: EUR 1.2M private equity led by Vendep Capital, announced 2017-08-23

technical_complexity.rationale: A matching and messaging layer over email, text and the web, connected to Eventbrite's ticketing data. Standard web engineering for a solo founder, no hard research problem.

defensibility.rationale: Event networking and matchmaking was already offered by funded vendors such as Brella, and an Eventbrite integration is easy to copy. No data or network effect was visible at founding.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found showing any incumbent copied or bought the product. Eventbrite itself offered no comparable attendee matching in the sources found.

market_need_then: Event organizers and sponsors valued engaged attendees and networking was a feature sold by dedicated vendors by 2017, but this research found no direct evidence of demand for the In The Room product itself.

branding.domain_note: Uses intheroom.social rather than an exact .com; no source on how it was obtained.

identity.visual_style: Minimal site with only a title and tagline when fetched
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and casual: Connect with people around you

branding.community_and_virality: No evidence found of merch, fan accounts or press about the brand itself.

brand_strength.rationale: The name is a common phrase shared with an unrelated London conversational AI company and other event firms. Searches surfaced several unrelated In The Room entities and no press about this brand.

outcome_analysis: The company is listed as active with one person and little public trace. No funding, press coverage or exit was found beyond a January 2025 item saying an In The Room software product would power a large marketing conference, which may or may not be the same company. With no traction data, the story is a solo founder building a small event networking tool in a space where funded rivals already existed.
notes: YC page lists the founding year as 2020 while the batch is Winter 2019, so founded_year 2018 is an approximation tied to the batch application and is unverified. Outcome search and funding searches found no relevant results, and funding is unknown, not zero. The Crunchbase and CB Insights snippets seen may describe different companies named In The Room. The January 2025 newsworthy.ai item was seen only as a search snippet and not verified as the same company.
